# The Sky That Will Not Fall

## Scripture
*"He set the earth on its foundations; it can never be moved." — Psalm 104:5 (NIV)*

## Reflection
Autumn evenings invite us to look up—and perhaps to steady ourselves. The ground beneath our feet feels fixed, but astronomers tell us our planet spins at roughly a thousand miles per hour while racing around the sun at sixty-seven thousand miles per hour. We are, in truth, riders on a whirling world.

Yet here is the wonder: God made it so. He anchored the earth with gravity and set it on foundations we cannot see, and in His design, motion and stability are not enemies. The same is true of us. Autumn arrives, leaves fall, schedules shift, and life spins faster than we'd like. We may feel untethered. But the God who holds a spinning globe steady also holds spinning lives.

The psalmist's confidence wasn't rooted in a still, motionless earth—it was rooted in the God whose word keeps it in place. When everything around us feels in upheaval, we rest not on our circumstances but on the One who fixed the foundations. He who established the world so firmly that it never falls from its course is faithful to keep you in yours.

Tonight, step outside. The ground feels solid because He made it so. Let that steadiness find its way into your soul—you are held by the same hand.

## Prayer
Lord, the world spins and seasons turn, yet You hold it all together. When life feels unsteady, remind me that Your faithfulness is my foundation. Keep me steady in Your hands tonight. Amen.
